title: The One at the End
subtitle: 城市生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 城市生活（社会服务与人际沟通·城市生活）
meta: 主题语境：城市生活（社会服务与人际沟通·城市生活）　|　核心词汇：block　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 block 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 my uncle lived on ① a block that had nine houses and one shop, and he said the shop was the whole of the street. The ② block, meaning the row and not the stone, was pulled down in March and was rebuilt in eleven months; a block, he said, is the only thing in a city that is mourned before it is gone.

Every ③ block in that town was known by a different name, and the ④ block at the end, meaning the one with the yard and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever chose. A block, my grandmother said, is nine parts neighbours and one part a shop you can walk to; my uncle said the neighbours are the part that changes.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ block was the whole of the wall, meaning the solid piece and not the row. The ⑥ block, meaning the single mass and not any of that, is the only thing in a building that everybody leans on and nobody looks at; a block, she said, is either a row of houses or the only word that means both a street and a lump. He said the lump came first.

By 1972 the ⑦ block had become a photograph in an archive, and the archive had become an argument about who had lived where. The ⑧ block of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in April, was nine houses and eleven years of neighbours; a block, he said, is either the row at the end or the reason you know which door is yours. She said the door was never the difficult part.

The ⑨ block I remember is the one at the end, which was demolished in 1975 and is still being described. A ⑩ block, my grandmother said in 1977, is the only thing in a city that improves by being remembered; every block, she said, is a lump that has agreed to look like a street. He said the lump was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 街区；一排房子
B. n. 街区（指那一排房子，与石头相对）
C. 固定搭配：live on a block 住在某个街区
D. n. 街区（指那个镇上每一个）
E. n. 街区（指尽头那一个）
F. n. 大块；整块（指墙上那块实心的材料）
G. n. 整块（抽象：那一整块实体）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a block that had nine houses and one shop
The block, meaning the row and not the stone
block was the whole of the wall
The block, meaning the single mass
the block had become a photograph in an archive
The block of the whole thing
A block, my grandmother said in 1977

answers.why: live on a block 意为“住在某个街区”，1954 年叔叔住在一个有九栋房子和一家店的街区。
block 意为“街区”，指那一排房子而不是石头，它三月被拆掉，十一个月后重建。
block 指那个镇上每一个街区，每一个都由不同的名字被人记住。
block 指尽头那一个（带院子的那一个），是唯一有人主动挑的。
block 意为“大块、整块”，指墙上那块实心的材料，母亲说 block 就是那堵墙的全部。
block 为抽象用法，指那一整块实体，是一栋建筑里人人都倚靠、却没人去看的东西。
block 意为“街区”，到 1972 年这个 block 成了档案馆里的一张照片。
block 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，叔叔四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九栋房子和十一年的邻居。
block 意为“街区”，我记得的是尽头那一个，1975 年被拆掉，至今还被人描述着。
block 为抽象总称，祖母说街区是城里唯一会因为被记住而变好的东西。
